question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

The storm passed ______, but the night remained warm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. quickly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank modifies the verb "passed" — it tells us how the storm passed. A verb is modified by an adverb, and the adverb formed from "quick" is "quickly". (शीघ्रता से)

◦ Correct: The storm passed quickly, but the night remained warm.

• Formation rule: adjective + -ly = adverb of manner (quick → quickly, slow → slowly, sudden → suddenly).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "quickest" is the superlative degree, which needs a comparison group and "the" (the quickest runner) — it cannot describe a single past action here.

• Option 2 "quicker" is the comparative degree and requires "than" (quicker than the last storm).

• Option 4 "quick" is an adjective; adjectives qualify nouns/pronouns (a quick storm), not verbs.

NOTE

• Adjective vs adverb is a very frequent SSC trap:

◦ Adjective → describes a noun: "It was a quick decision."

◦ Adverb → describes a verb/adjective/another adverb: "He decided quickly."

• Watch out for words that are the same in both forms — fast, hard, late, early, straight ("He runs fast", not "fastly").

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

The tourists (rendered to the) museum on time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. arrived at the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence needs a verb meaning "reached (a place)". The correct expression is "arrived at" — used with a specific, comparatively small place such as a museum, station, office or airport. (पहुँचना)

◦ Correct: The tourists arrived at the museum on time.

• "Rendered" means to give, provide or present (render help, render a service) and is completely unsuitable here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "appeared at the" means "showed up/became visible", which does not convey the sense of reaching a destination punctually and is unidiomatic with "on time".

• Option 2 "occurred to the" means "came into someone's mind" (An idea occurred to me) — it is used with a person, not a place.

• Option 3 "No correction required" is wrong because "rendered to the museum" is meaningless.

NOTE

• Prepositions with arrive:

◦ arrive at + small/specific place — arrive at the museum, arrive at the station, arrive at school.

◦ arrive in + large place (city, country) — arrive in Delhi, arrive in India.

◦ Never use "arrive to". Also note: reach takes no preposition — "reach the museum".

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

The number of homes with running watered has been rising sharply since 1985.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. with running water.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Running water" is a fixed collocation meaning water supplied through pipes/taps. Here "running" is a present participle used as an adjective qualifying the noun "water". (नल का बहता पानी)

◦ Correct: The number of homes with running water has been rising sharply since 1985.

• "Watered" is a past participle/verb form and cannot function as the noun after the preposition "with".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "with run water" uses the base verb "run", which cannot pre-modify a noun in this sense.

• Option 3 "of ran watered" is doubly wrong — "ran" is a past tense form (never used as an adjective) and "of" is the wrong preposition here.

• Option 4 "No improvement" is wrong because "with running watered" is ungrammatical.

NOTE

• Present participle (V-ing) as adjective describes something doing the action: running water, boiling milk, a flying bird, a sleeping child.

• Past participle (V3) as adjective describes something that receives the action: boiled milk, broken glass, watered plants.

• Note the tense too: "has been rising ... since 1985" — present perfect continuous with since + point of time is correct.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Unless you complete your school education, you cannot get yourself ______ into a college.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. enrolled.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Enrol/enroll" means to officially register or admit oneself as a member/student of an institution. The collocation "enrolled into/in a college" fits the context of admission after completing school education. (नामांकित होना / प्रवेश लेना)

◦ Correct: Unless you complete your school education, you cannot get yourself enrolled into a college.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "advanced" means moved forward/promoted — one is not "advanced into a college".

• Option 3 "mopped" means cleaned a floor with a mop — entirely unrelated.

• Option 4 "accommodated" means provided with lodging or adjusted to fit; a college admits students, it does not "accommodate" them into itself.

NOTE

• Related words: enrolment/enrollment (noun), enrolee (one who enrols).

• "Unless" = "if ... not". It already carries a negative sense, so never add another "not" after it: "Unless you study, you will fail" (NOT "Unless you do not study").

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

No matter how mountains are formed, they eventually becomes too heavy and succumb to gravity.
option_3: too heavy and succumb to gravity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. formed, they eventually becomes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject–verb agreement rule is violated. The subject "they" (referring to the plural noun "mountains") is plural, so the verb must be the plural form "become", not the singular "becomes".

◦ Correct: No matter how mountains are formed, they eventually become too heavy and succumb to gravity.

• Confirmation: the parallel verb later in the sentence is "succumb" (plural form), proving the subject is plural.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No matter how mountains are" is correct — "No matter how" introduces a concessive clause, and "are formed" is correct passive voice.

• Option 3 "too heavy and succumb to gravity." is correct — "too + adjective" and "succumb to" are both right.

• Option 4 "No error" is wrong since the error lies in Part 1.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: singular subject → verb with -s/-es (he becomes); plural subject → base verb (they become).

• "Succumb to" means to yield/give in to something stronger (succumb to pressure, succumb to injuries).

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

Dead men's shoes
option_1: Making oneself available for all the tasks being assigned
option_2: A career where a lot of cheques are signed
option_3: Job that one takes over from somebody who has left unexpectedly or died
option_4: Acquiring the wealth of a dead man through malpractices
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Job that one takes over from somebody who has left unexpectedly or died.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "dead men's shoes" refers to a position, job or property that becomes available only when the previous holder leaves suddenly, retires or dies. It suggests promotion that can come only through someone else's departure. (किसी के हटने/मरने पर ही खाली होने वाला पद)

◦ Example: In that old firm, promotion was strictly a matter of waiting for dead men's shoes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 describes willingness to work, not the idiom's meaning.

• Option 2 is a play on "cheques being signed" and has no connection with the phrase.

• Option 4 wrongly suggests dishonest acquisition of wealth; the idiom carries no sense of malpractice.

NOTE

• Related workplace idioms often asked in SSC exams:

◦ "Step into someone's shoes" — to take over another person's role/duties.

◦ "In someone's shoes" — in another person's situation.

◦ "Waiting in the wings" — ready to take over when the chance comes.

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Arrogance
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Dominance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Arrogance" means an offensive display of superiority, haughtiness and overbearing pride. Among the given choices, "dominance" — the exercise of power and superiority over others — is the closest in sense. (घमंड / अहंकार / प्रभुत्व)

◦ Example: His arrogance/dominance over his juniors made him unpopular.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Inhibition" means a feeling that makes one self-conscious and unable to act freely — the opposite kind of trait.

• Option 2 "Bashful" means shy and easily embarrassed; it is also an adjective, whereas the question word is a noun.

• Option 4 "Diffidence" means lack of self-confidence, shyness — a direct antonym of arrogance.

NOTE

• Synonyms of arrogance: haughtiness, hubris, conceit, insolence, superciliousness, imperiousness.

• Antonyms of arrogance: humility, modesty, diffidence, meekness.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

Richard Dawkins written the foreword to the second edition of the book.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. wrote the foreword.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Written" is the past participle (V3) of "write" and can never stand alone as the main verb — it needs an auxiliary (has/have/had/was). Since no auxiliary is present, the sentence requires the simple past (V2) "wrote", which describes a completed past action.

◦ Correct: Richard Dawkins wrote the foreword to the second edition of the book.

• Verb forms: write – wrote – written.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "will wrote the foreword" is wrong — after the modal "will", only the base form (V1) is used ("will write").

• Option 3 "write the foreword" is wrong because the third-person singular subject in the present tense would need "writes", and the sense here is clearly of a completed past act.

• Option 4 "No improvement" is wrong since "written" without a helping verb is ungrammatical.

NOTE

• A "foreword" is an introductory note written for a book, usually by someone other than the author (do not confuse it with "forward", meaning ahead).

• After modals (will, shall, can, may, must, should) always use V1; after have/has/had and in the passive, use V3.

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Before he could devote many more / thought to the matter, Pranav / had stepped up to him.
option_1: Before he could devote many more
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Before he could devote many more.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Thought" here is an uncountable (abstract) noun meaning "consideration/mental attention". Uncountable nouns take "much", not "many". Hence "many more thought" must be "much more thought".

◦ Correct: Before he could devote much more thought to the matter, Pranav had stepped up to him.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "thought to the matter, Pranav" is correct — "devote something to something" is the right collocation.

• Option 3 "had stepped up to him." is correct — the past perfect shows the action that happened first, matching "Before ... could".

• Option 4 "No error" is wrong because Part 1 contains the quantifier error.

NOTE

• Many + plural countable nouns: many books, many thoughts, many ideas.

• Much + uncountable nouns: much water, much information, much thought, much advice.

• Common uncountable nouns in SSC exams: information, advice, furniture, luggage, scenery, machinery, equipment, news, poetry, work.

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

There is no need to attack our guest.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. assault.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Attack" means to act violently against someone; to assail or criticise aggressively. Its closest synonym is "assault", which likewise means to make a violent physical or verbal attack. (हमला करना)

◦ Example: There is no need to attack/assault our guest.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "generate" means to produce or create (generate electricity) — unrelated.

• Option 3 "mark" means to make a sign on something, or to notice/grade — unrelated.

• Option 4 "adore" means to love and admire deeply — a clear antonym in this context.

NOTE

• Synonyms of attack: assault, assail, strike, storm, charge, ambush, invade.

• Antonyms of attack: defend, protect, shield, guard, retreat.

• "Assault" is also a legal term for the offence of threatening or applying unlawful force to a person.

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

Oak trees do not use leaves to make food ______ the winter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. during.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "During" is a preposition meaning throughout the course of a period of time, and it is followed by a noun ("the winter"). It correctly expresses that the process continues over the whole winter season. (के दौरान)

◦ Correct: Oak trees do not use leaves to make food during the winter.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "while" is a conjunction and must be followed by a clause (subject + verb), e.g., "while it is winter" — not by the bare noun "the winter".

• Option 2 "within" means "inside the limits of" and normally indicates a deadline (within a week), which distorts the meaning.

• Option 4 "by" indicates a point of time before which something happens (by winter), not a continuing period.

NOTE

• during + noun (during the holidays) vs while + clause (while we were on holiday).

• for + length of time (for three months) vs during + named period (during the monsoon).

• Oak trees are deciduous — they shed their leaves in autumn and hence cannot photosynthesise in winter.

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Maintaen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Maintaen" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "maintain", meaning to keep something in good condition, or to continue/assert something. (बनाए रखना)

◦ Spelling key: MAIN + TAIN. Remember it contains the word "main" followed by "-tain".

◦ Example: We must maintain the machines regularly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Boring" (dull/uninteresting), "Stupid" (foolish) and "Gang" (an organised group) are all spelt correctly.

NOTE

• Word family: maintain (verb) → maintenance (noun — note the change to "-tenance", a very common spelling error) → maintainable (adjective).

• Other "-tain" verbs: contain, retain, obtain, sustain, entertain, attain.

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: He stuod outside the bathroom door.
option_2: He stood outcide the bathroom door.
option_3: He stood outside the bathroom door.
option_4: He stood outside the bathrum door.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. He stood outside the bathroom door.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• All three key words are correctly spelt in Option 3 — "stood" (past tense of stand), "outside" and "bathroom".

◦ Correct: He stood outside the bathroom door.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 misspells "stood" as "stuod" (the vowels are reversed).

• Option 2 misspells "outside" as "outcide" (s is wrongly replaced by c).

• Option 4 misspells "bathroom" as "bathrum" (the compound is bath + room).

NOTE

• Verb forms: stand – stood – stood.

• "Outside" = out + side (opposite: inside). Compound nouns keep both full words: bath + room = bathroom, bed + room = bedroom, class + room = classroom.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

One who hates war, loves peace
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Pacifist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "pacifist" is a person who believes that war and violence are unjustifiable and who loves and works for peace. (शांतिवादी)

◦ Example: As a committed pacifist, he refused to join the army.

• The word comes from Latin pax/pacis = peace.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Desecrater" means one who violates or profanes something sacred.

• Option 3 "Fatalist" means one who believes that all events are predetermined by fate and cannot be changed.

• Option 4 "Conformist" means one who follows accepted rules, customs and standards without question.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes frequently asked in SSC:

◦ Belligerent — one who is engaged in war/aggressively hostile.

◦ Mercenary — a soldier who fights for money for a foreign army.

◦ Misanthrope — one who hates mankind; Philanthropist — one who loves and helps mankind.

question:
Choose the word that is opposite in meaning to the given word.

Lordly
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Ignoble.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lordly" means grand, noble, majestic, befitting a lord (and, in another sense, haughty). Its antonym is "ignoble", meaning not honourable, base, of low character or humble birth. (नीच / अधम)

◦ Example: His lordly bearing contrasted sharply with his ignoble conduct.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Despair" is a noun/verb meaning complete loss of hope — not an antonym of a quality adjective like lordly.

• Option 2 "Arrogant" is a synonym of lordly in its "haughty" sense.

• Option 4 "Saucy" means impudent, cheeky or bold — again closer to the haughty sense than opposite to it.

NOTE

• Prefix "ig-/in-/im-/il-/ir-" means "not": ignoble (not noble), ignorant, inactive, impossible, illegal, irregular.

• Synonyms of lordly: noble, majestic, grand, aristocratic, imperious. Antonyms: ignoble, humble, lowly, modest.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

The lion's share
option_2: To lose a big amount of money
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The largest portion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "the lion's share" means the largest or greatest part of something. (सबसे बड़ा हिस्सा)

◦ Example: The eldest brother took the lion's share of the property.

• Origin: it comes from one of Aesop's fables, in which the lion claims most of the hunted prey for himself.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Life with no regrets" has no link with the phrase.

• Option 2 "To lose a big amount of money" is closer to idioms like "lose one's shirt".

• Option 3 "Big success" would correspond to idioms such as "a roaring success" or "hit the jackpot".

NOTE

• Other animal idioms often asked in SSC:

◦ "Lion-hearted" — very brave.

◦ "Beard the lion in his den" — to confront a powerful person on his own ground.

◦ "The lion's den" — a dangerous or hostile place.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Black holes can has powerful effects on their surroundings.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. has powerful effects.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After a modal auxiliary such as "can", the verb must be in the base form (V1). Therefore "can has" is wrong; it should be "can have".

◦ Correct: Black holes can have powerful effects on their surroundings.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No error" is wrong because the modal + V1 rule is violated.

• Option 3 "on their surroundings." is correct — "effect on" is the right preposition and "their" agrees with the plural "black holes".

• Option 4 "Black holes can" is correct as the subject + modal.

NOTE

• Modal + V1 always: can go, may write, must have, should be, will take, could see.

• Do not confuse "effect" (noun — result: the effect of heat) with "affect" (verb — to influence: heat affects metals).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The priest puts some ______ water on the child's head.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. holy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Holy" means sacred, consecrated, associated with God or religion. "Holy water" is water blessed by a priest and used in religious ceremonies, which fits the context perfectly. (पवित्र जल)

◦ Correct: The priest puts some holy water on the child's head.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "hairy" means covered with hair — meaningless with water.

• Option 3 "haughty" means arrogantly proud; it describes people, not water.

• Option 4 "wholly" is an adverb meaning "entirely/completely" and cannot qualify the noun "water".

NOTE

• Note the near-homophones: holy (sacred) / wholly (entirely) / holey (full of holes) / holly (a plant).

• The ceremony described — sprinkling holy water on a child's head — is a baptism/christening.

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

The freedom to browse a secure and accountable online space will be compromised.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. irresponsible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Accountable" means responsible; required to explain and justify one's actions. Its antonym is "irresponsible", meaning not answerable and showing no sense of responsibility. (जवाबदेह का विलोम — गैर-ज़िम्मेदार)

◦ Example: An accountable administration answers to the people; an irresponsible one does not.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "indebted" means owing money or gratitude — unrelated to accountability.

• Option 2 "amicable" means friendly and peaceable (an amicable settlement) — unrelated.

• Option 4 "liable" means legally responsible/likely to — a synonym rather than an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of accountable: responsible, answerable, liable, obligated.

• Antonyms of accountable: irresponsible, unaccountable, exempt, immune.

• Negative prefix "ir-" is used before words beginning with r: irresponsible, irregular, irrational, irrelevant, irreversible.

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

An exact copy of handwriting, printing
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Facsimile.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "facsimile" is an exact copy or reproduction of writing, printing, a picture or a document. (प्रतिकृति / हूबहू नकल)

◦ Example: The museum displays a facsimile of the original manuscript.

• The word comes from Latin fac simile = "make similar"; the modern word "fax" is a shortening of facsimile.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Platitude" means a dull, over-used remark stated as if it were new.

• Option 2 "Maiden" means an unmarried girl, or "first of its kind" (maiden speech, maiden voyage).

• Option 3 "Potable" means fit to drink (potable water).

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes:

◦ Replica — an exact copy or model of an object.

◦ Forgery — a fraudulent copy made to deceive.

◦ Manuscript — a handwritten or typed document; Transcript — a written copy of spoken material.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

In a gallery at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (1)______ New York, paintings of a father and daughter (2)______ face to face. Larger than life, the monumental portraits (3)______ competing conceptions of royal power. The father, Henry VIII, (4)______ directly at the viewer, conveying aggression through his wide stance, bulging leg muscles and (5)______ padded clothing.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. in.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "in" is used with large places such as cities, states and countries. Since New York is a city, the correct phrase is "the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York".

◦ Correct: In a gallery at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, paintings of a father and daughter hang face to face.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "to" shows direction/movement (going to New York), not location.

• Option 3 "on" is used for surfaces, streets and dates (on the table, on Monday).

• Option 4 "at" is used for specific points/small places (at the museum, at the gate) — indeed the passage already uses "at the Metropolitan Museum of Art"; the city that follows needs "in".

NOTE

• Prepositions of place — the ladder rule:

◦ in → large areas: in India, in Delhi, in the room.

◦ on → surfaces/lines: on the wall, on the road, on the floor.

◦ at → exact points: at the corner, at the bus stop, at 5 p.m.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

In a gallery at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (1)______ New York, paintings of a father and daughter (2)______ face to face. Larger than life, the monumental portraits (3)______ competing conceptions of royal power. The father, Henry VIII, (4)______ directly at the viewer, conveying aggression through his wide stance, bulging leg muscles and (5)______ padded clothing.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. hang.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hang" is the correct verb for paintings displayed on a wall, and the plural subject "paintings" requires the plural verb form "hang".

◦ Correct: ... paintings of a father and daughter hang face to face.

• Verb forms: hang – hung – hung (for objects).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "rest" would suggest the paintings are lying/supported on something, not mounted on a wall facing each other.

• Option 3 "poised" is a past participle/adjective; without an auxiliary ("are poised") it cannot serve as the main verb here.

• Option 4 "hanged" is used only for the execution of a person by hanging (the criminal was hanged) — never for objects.

NOTE

• The distinction is a classic SSC question:

◦ hang – hung – hung → to suspend an object: "The picture was hung on the wall."

◦ hang – hanged – hanged → to put a person to death: "The murderer was hanged at dawn."

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

In a gallery at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (1)______ New York, paintings of a father and daughter (2)______ face to face. Larger than life, the monumental portraits (3)______ competing conceptions of royal power. The father, Henry VIII, (4)______ directly at the viewer, conveying aggression through his wide stance, bulging leg muscles and (5)______ padded clothing.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. present.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Present" here means to display, portray or set forth for the viewer. The two monumental portraits present (put forward) competing ideas of royal power. (प्रस्तुत करना)

◦ Correct: Larger than life, the monumental portraits present competing conceptions of royal power.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "believe" needs a thinking, animate subject — paintings cannot believe anything.

• Option 2 "sell" makes no sense with abstract "conceptions of royal power".

• Option 4 "settle" means to resolve or make stable, which contradicts the word "competing" (i.e., rival, unsettled ideas).

NOTE

• "Present" is a heteronym: as a verb it is stressed on the second syllable (pre-SENT = to offer/display); as a noun/adjective on the first (PRE-sent = a gift / currently existing).

• Useful synonyms in this sense: portray, depict, put forward, showcase, exhibit.

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

In a gallery at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (1)______ New York, paintings of a father and daughter (2)______ face to face. Larger than life, the monumental portraits (3)______ competing conceptions of royal power. The father, Henry VIII, (4)______ directly at the viewer, conveying aggression through his wide stance, bulging leg muscles and (5)______ padded clothing.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. looks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage says Henry VIII gazes "directly at the viewer". The verb that collocates with "directly at" is "look", and the singular subject "The father, Henry VIII" takes the singular verb "looks". (देखता है)

◦ Correct: The father, Henry VIII, looks directly at the viewer, conveying aggression ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "books" (to reserve) and Option 4 "hooks" (to fasten with a hook) are meaningless with "directly at the viewer".

• Option 2 "shocks" would need a direct object without "at" (shocks the viewer), so the preposition rules it out.

NOTE

• Verbs of seeing: look at (deliberately direct one's eyes), see (perceive), watch (observe something moving over time).

• Subject–verb agreement: the appositive "Henry VIII" does not change the singular subject "The father" — hence "looks".

question:
In the following passage some of the words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the correct answer for the given blank out of the four alternatives.

In a gallery at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (1)______ New York, paintings of a father and daughter (2)______ face to face. Larger than life, the monumental portraits (3)______ competing conceptions of royal power. The father, Henry VIII, (4)______ directly at the viewer, conveying aggression through his wide stance, bulging leg muscles and (5)______ padded clothing.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. excessively.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage stresses exaggerated aggression — "larger than life", "wide stance", "bulging leg muscles". The adverb "excessively" (to an extreme, more than necessary) matches this sense of over-emphasised bulk in the clothing. (अत्यधिक)

◦ Correct: ... conveying aggression through his wide stance, bulging leg muscles and excessively padded clothing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "totally" means completely/entirely and does not convey the idea of "more than needed".

• Option 3 "commonly" means usually/frequently, which weakens rather than heightens the description.

• Option 4 "acutely" means sharply or intensely and is normally used with feelings or senses (acutely aware, acutely painful), not with padding.

NOTE

• Synonyms of excessively: exorbitantly, inordinately, unduly, extravagantly, immoderately.

• Adverbs of degree modify adjectives/participles: excessively padded, heavily embroidered, richly decorated.

question: Who is the author of the novel 'The God of Small Things'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arundhati Roy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The God of Small Things" (1997) was written by Arundhati Roy. It won her the Booker Prize in 1997, making her the first Indian woman to win the award. (अरुंधति रॉय)

• The novel is set in Aymanam, Kerala, and tells the story of the twins Rahel and Estha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Khushwant Singh — "Train to Pakistan", "The Company of Women", "Delhi".

• Aravind Adiga — "The White Tiger" (Booker Prize 2008).

• Kiran Desai — "The Inheritance of Loss" (Booker Prize 2006); her mother Anita Desai was shortlisted three times.

NOTE

• Indian-origin Booker winners: V. S. Naipaul (1971), Salman Rushdie (1981), Arundhati Roy (1997), Kiran Desai (2006), Aravind Adiga (2008).

• Arundhati Roy's second novel is "The Ministry of Utmost Happiness" (2017); she is also known for her political essays.

question: The Governor of a State shall, after every ________ years, constitute a finance commission under Article 243-I of the Indian Constitution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is five.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 243-I of the Constitution, the Governor of a State shall constitute a State Finance Commission at the expiration of every fifth year to review the financial position of the Panchayats. (राज्य वित्त आयोग — हर पाँच वर्ष)

• It recommends how taxes, duties, tolls and fees should be distributed between the State and the Panchayats, and what grants-in-aid should be given.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 243-I falls in Part IX (The Panchayats), inserted by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.

• Article 243-Y requires the same State Finance Commission to review the finances of Municipalities (Part IX-A, added by the 74th Amendment, 1992).

• The Union Finance Commission is constituted by the President under Article 280, also every fifth year.

NOTE

• Key Panchayati Raj articles: 243B (constitution of Panchayats), 243C (composition), 243D (reservation of seats), 243E (five-year term), 243G (powers), 243K (State Election Commission).

question: Festival of “Hola Mohalla” is celebrated by which community?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hola Mohalla" is a festival of the Sikh community, celebrated chiefly at Anandpur Sahib in Punjab, on the day after Holi (in the month of Chet). (होला मोहल्ला — सिख समुदाय)

• It was started by Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru, in 1701, as an occasion for the display of martial skills — mock battles, Gatka (sword-fighting), horsemanship and archery — by the Nihangs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other major Sikh festivals: Baisakhi (founding of the Khalsa in 1699), Guru Nanak Jayanti (Gurpurab), Bandi Chhor Divas.

• Jain festivals: Mahavir Jayanti, Paryushana. Parsi: Navroz, Pateti. Buddhist: Buddha Purnima, Losar.

NOTE

• Anandpur Sahib, founded by Guru Tegh Bahadur, is one of the holiest places of Sikhism and the birthplace of the Khalsa.

question: As of 2022, India is the ______ largest producer of wheat in the world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is second.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As of 2022, India is the second largest producer of wheat in the world, after China. (गेहूँ उत्पादन में भारत दूसरे स्थान पर)

• Wheat is India's second most important food crop after rice and is the main rabi crop.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Leading wheat-producing states of India: Uttar Pradesh (largest), Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan.

• Wheat requires a cool growing season and bright sunshine at ripening; 50–75 cm of annual rainfall is ideal.

• India is also the second largest producer of rice, sugarcane, groundnut and cotton, and the largest producer of milk, pulses, jute, spices and bananas.

NOTE

• Rabi crops are sown in October–December and harvested in April–June: wheat, barley, gram, mustard, peas.

• Kharif crops are sown with the onset of the monsoon (June–July): rice, maize, jowar, bajra, cotton.

question: Who among the following won a gold medal in weightlifting in commonwealth Games 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saikhom Mirabai Chanu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Saikhom Mirabai Chanu won the gold medal in weightlifting (women's 49 kg) at the Commonwealth Games 2022 held in Birmingham, England. (मीराबाई चानू — स्वर्ण पदक)

• She lifted a Games-record total of 201 kg (88 kg snatch + 113 kg clean and jerk).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The others named also won medals at Birmingham 2022 but not gold: Sanket Sagar (silver, men's 55 kg), Bindyarani Devi (silver, women's 55 kg) and Vikas Thakur (silver, men's 96 kg).

• Mirabai Chanu won a silver medal at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021) — India's first medal of those Games — and gold at the 2017 World Weightlifting Championships.

NOTE

• She hails from Manipur and has received the Khel Ratna, Padma Shri (2018) and the Arjuna Award.

• The Commonwealth Games 2022 were held in Birmingham; India finished with 61 medals (22 gold, 16 silver, 23 bronze).

question: Which is the second highest mountain in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kamet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kamet" (7,756 m) is the second highest peak in the Garhwal Himalaya of Uttarakhand, after Nanda Devi (7,816 m). (कामेट — गढ़वाल का दूसरा सर्वोच्च शिखर)

• It lies in the Chamoli district, close to the Tibet border, and was first climbed in 1931 by a British team led by Frank Smythe.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nanda Devi (7,816 m) is the highest peak entirely within India and the second highest in the country after Kangchenjunga (8,586 m).

• Nilkantha (6,596 m) towers above Badrinath, and Mount Meru (6,660 m) is famous for the "Shark's Fin" climbing route.

NOTE

• The Nanda Devi National Park and Valley of Flowers are UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Uttarakhand.

• Other Garhwal peaks: Trisul, Chaukhamba, Bandarpunch, Satopanth and Shivling.

question: The British parliament transferred the powers of east India company to the British crown in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1858.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• By the Government of India Act, 1858, the British Parliament abolished the East India Company's rule and transferred all its powers to the British Crown. (1858 — शासन ब्रिटिश ताज को हस्तांतरित)

• The Act was passed in the aftermath of the Revolt of 1857. It abolished the Board of Control and the Court of Directors, created the office of the Secretary of State for India (assisted by a 15-member Council of India) and renamed the Governor-General as the Viceroy — Lord Canning being the first.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• 1773 — Regulating Act: the first step in British parliamentary control; made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings).

• 1909 — Morley-Minto Reforms: introduced separate electorates for Muslims.

• 1919 — Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms: introduced dyarchy in the provinces.

NOTE

• The Act of 1858 is also called the "Act for the Good Government of India"; Queen Victoria's Proclamation of 1 November 1858 announced the change at Allahabad.

question: Which among the following features of the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the Constitution of Britain?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cabinet System.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Cabinet System (i.e., the parliamentary form of government) was borrowed from the Constitution of Britain (the United Kingdom). (मंत्रिमंडल प्रणाली — ब्रिटेन से)

• Other features taken from Britain: rule of law, single citizenship, bicameralism, the legislative procedure, the office of the Speaker, prerogative writs and the parliamentary privileges.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Directive Principles of State Policy — borrowed from Ireland.

• Fundamental Duties — borrowed from the erstwhile USSR (Russia); added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976 (Article 51A).

• Concurrent List — borrowed from Australia (along with freedom of trade and commerce and the joint sitting of the two Houses).

NOTE

• Other borrowings: Fundamental Rights, judicial review and impeachment of the President — USA; Emergency provisions — Germany (Weimar); Federal system with a strong Centre and residuary powers — Canada; Amendment procedure and Rajya Sabha members' nomination — South Africa; Directive Principles' procedure established by law — Japan.

question: Who among the following won the Mexican Formula 1 Grand Prix 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Max Verstappen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Max Verstappen (Netherlands), driving for Red Bull Racing, won the Mexico City Grand Prix (Mexican Formula 1 Grand Prix) 2022 at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. (मैक्स वेरस्टापेन)

• With this win he set a new record for the most wins in a single Formula 1 season (14 wins in 2022).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Max Verstappen won the F1 World Drivers' Championship in 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024.

• Carlos Sainz Jr. and Charles Leclerc drove for Ferrari in 2022, while Lando Norris drove for McLaren.

NOTE

• Formula One is governed by the FIA (Federation Internationale de l'Automobile).

• The Indian Grand Prix was held at the Buddh International Circuit, Greater Noida, from 2011 to 2013.

question: Plants require nutrients for their growth which can be supplied through ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Soil, water and air.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Plants obtain their nutrients from soil, water and air. (मिट्टी, जल और वायु)

◦ From the air they take carbon dioxide (the source of carbon and oxygen).

◦ From water they get hydrogen and oxygen.

◦ From the soil they absorb mineral nutrients — nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium, sulphur and micronutrients — through their roots.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Macronutrients required in large amounts: C, H, O, N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S.

• Micronutrients required in traces: Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu, B, Mo, Cl.

• Plants prepare their own food by photosynthesis: 6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2 (in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll).

NOTE

• Nitrogen cannot be taken directly from the air by most plants; it is fixed by Rhizobium bacteria in the root nodules of leguminous plants and by lightning.

• Deficiency of nitrogen causes chlorosis (yellowing of leaves).

question: Which of the following is 'NOT' an example of communicable diseases?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Diabetes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Diabetes" is a non-communicable (non-infectious) disease — it is a metabolic disorder caused by the inadequate production or ineffective use of insulin by the pancreas, and it does not spread from person to person. (मधुमेह — असंचारी रोग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Chicken Pox — caused by the Varicella-zoster virus; spreads through air/contact.

• Common cold — caused by rhinoviruses; spreads through droplets.

• Tuberculosis (TB) — caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis; spreads through air; the BCG vaccine protects against it.

NOTE

• Communicable diseases spread through air (TB, influenza), water (cholera, typhoid), vectors (malaria, dengue) and contact (AIDS, hepatitis B).

• Other non-communicable diseases: cancer, hypertension, heart disease, arthritis, obesity.

• Insulin was discovered by Banting and Best; it lowers blood glucose, while glucagon raises it.

question: Which famous Indian Odissi dancer received the Padma Vibhushan, India's second highest civilian award, in 2000?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kelucharan Mohapatra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, the legendary Odissi dancer and guru from Odisha, was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2000. (केलुचरण महापात्र — पद्म विभूषण, 2000)

• He is credited with reviving and codifying Odissi as a classical dance form in the twentieth century, and had earlier received the Padma Shri (1972) and Padma Bhushan (1988).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Darshana Jhaveri is an exponent of Manipuri dance (one of the famous Jhaveri sisters).

• Sunanda Nair is known for Mohiniyattam.

• Rukmini Devi Arundale was a Bharatanatyam exponent and founder of Kalakshetra, Chennai.

NOTE

• Odissi is the classical dance of Odisha, characterised by the tribhanga posture and chowk stance; it draws inspiration from the sculptures of the Konark and Jagannath temples.

• Civilian awards in order: Bharat Ratna > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri.

question: Which among the following statements is incorrect?
option_1: Cell wall is present in animals.
option_2: Cell membrane is also called the plasma membrane.
option_3: Chromosomes are composed of DNA and Protein.
option_4: Mitochondria are known as the powerhouse of the cell.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cell wall is present in animals.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The statement "Cell wall is present in animals" is incorrect. A cell wall is absent in animal cells; it is found in plant cells (made of cellulose), as well as in bacteria (peptidoglycan) and fungi (chitin). (कोशिका भित्ति जंतु कोशिका में नहीं होती)

• Animal cells are bounded only by a flexible plasma membrane, which is why they can take various shapes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Statement 2 is correct — the cell membrane is also called the plasma membrane; it is selectively permeable and is described by the fluid mosaic model (Singer and Nicolson, 1972).

• Statement 3 is correct — chromosomes are made of DNA and histone proteins (chromatin).

• Statement 4 is correct — mitochondria are the "powerhouse of the cell" because they produce ATP through cellular respiration.

NOTE

• Structures present in plant cells but absent in animal cells: cell wall, plastids (chloroplast) and a large central vacuole.

• Structures present in animal cells but generally absent in plant cells: centrioles and lysosomes (lysosomes are called "suicide bags").

question: Which among the following is the sole note issuing authority in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reserve Bank of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the sole note issuing authority in India. Under Section 22 of the RBI Act, 1934, it has the exclusive right to issue currency notes of all denominations except the one-rupee note and coins, which are issued by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India. (भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक — नोट जारी करने वाला एकमात्र प्राधिकरण)

• The RBI issues notes under the Minimum Reserve System (since 1957), keeping a minimum reserve of Rs 200 crore (Rs 115 crore in gold and Rs 85 crore in foreign securities).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• RBI was established on 1 April 1935 on the recommendation of the Hilton Young Commission and was nationalised in 1949. Its headquarters are in Mumbai; the first Governor was Sir Osborne Smith and the first Indian Governor was C. D. Deshmukh.

• IFCI (1948) was India's first development financial institution; NPCI (2008) operates retail payment systems such as UPI, RuPay, IMPS and NACH; SBI is a commercial bank.

NOTE

• Currency notes bear the signature of the RBI Governor, while the one-rupee note bears that of the Finance Secretary.

• Other functions of the RBI: banker to the government, banker's bank, controller of credit, custodian of foreign exchange reserves and lender of last resort.

question: Charkula is a famous dance form associated with which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Charkula" is a famous folk dance of the Braj region of Uttar Pradesh (Mathura–Vrindavan area). (चरकुला — उत्तर प्रदेश)

• In this dance a woman balances a large multi-tiered wooden pyramid (charkula) fitted with 108 lighted oil lamps on her head and dances to the accompaniment of Rasiya songs dedicated to Lord Krishna.

• It is traditionally performed on the third day after Holi, celebrating the birth of Radha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Uttar Pradesh: Raslila, Nautanki, Khyal, Dhobiya, Kajri, Jhora.

• Tamil Nadu — Karagattam, Kummi, Kolattam, Oyilattam.

• Tripura — Hojagiri, Garia, Lebang Boomani. Andhra Pradesh — Kuchipudi (classical), Burrakatha, Veeranatyam.

NOTE

• India's eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam received which of the following awards in the year 1998?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Padma Bhushan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam, the celebrated Kuchipudi dancer and guru, was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 1998. (वेम्पति चिन्ना सत्यम — पद्म भूषण, 1998)

• He founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy in Chennai (1963), choreographed numerous dance dramas, and is credited with taking Kuchipudi to the world stage. He had earlier received the Padma Shri (1970).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kuchipudi originates from the village of Kuchipudi in Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh; it was systematised by Siddhendra Yogi.

• Distinctive items of Kuchipudi include the Tarangam, in which the dancer performs on the rim of a brass plate, often balancing a pot of water on the head.

NOTE

• Order of civilian honours: Bharat Ratna (highest) > Padma Vibhushan > Padma Bhushan > Padma Shri. They were instituted in 1954.

• Other famous Kuchipudi exponents: Raja and Radha Reddy, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Shobha Naidu.

question: Cricket World Cup, 1983 was held in which of the following places?
solution_text:
The correct answer is England.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 1983 Cricket World Cup (Prudential Cup) was held in England. (1983 विश्व कप — इंग्लैंड)

• India, captained by Kapil Dev, won the title by defeating the West Indies by 43 runs in the final at Lord's, London, on 25 June 1983. India scored 183 and bowled out the West Indies for 140.

• Mohinder Amarnath was adjudged Man of the Match in both the semi-final and the final.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The first three World Cups (1975, 1979, 1983) were all hosted by England and played in the 60-over format.

• The West Indies had won the first two World Cups (1975 and 1979).

• Kapil Dev's unbeaten 175 against Zimbabwe at Tunbridge Wells in that tournament is legendary.

NOTE

• India's other World Cup titles: 2011 (ODI, at home, under M. S. Dhoni), 2007 (T20, under Dhoni) and 2024 (T20, under Rohit Sharma).

• Cricket's world body is the ICC (International Cricket Council), headquartered in Dubai.

question: With which neighbouring country does India share the Sunderbans forest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bangladesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, is shared by India (West Bengal) and Bangladesh. (सुंदरवन — भारत और बांग्लादेश)

• It lies in the delta of the Ganga, Brahmaputra and Meghna rivers on the Bay of Bengal, and is famous for the Royal Bengal Tiger.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sundarbans National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987), a Tiger Reserve (1973), a Biosphere Reserve (1989) and a Ramsar site (2019).

• The name is believed to come from the "Sundari" tree (Heritiera fomes), a dominant mangrove species there.

• Mangrove species have breathing roots (pneumatophores) and show vivipary (seeds germinate on the parent plant).

NOTE

• India shares land borders with 7 countries: Bangladesh (longest, ~4,096 km), China, Pakistan, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan and Afghanistan.

• Indian states bordering Bangladesh: West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

question: As per census 2011, what is the Total Fertility Rate in India? (provide an approximate range)
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.1-2.9.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Around the time of Census 2011, India's Total Fertility Rate (TFR) was approximately 2.4, which falls within the range 2.1–2.9. (कुल प्रजनन दर — लगभग 2.4)

• TFR is defined as the average number of children a woman would bear during her entire reproductive span (15–49 years) at prevailing age-specific fertility rates.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A TFR of about 2.1 is called the replacement level fertility — the level at which a population exactly replaces itself.

• As per NFHS-5 (2019–21), India's TFR has fallen to 2.0, below the replacement level.

• Census 2011 figures: population 121.08 crore; sex ratio 943; literacy rate 74.04%; density 382 persons per sq km.

NOTE

• Related demographic terms: Crude Birth Rate (CBR) — births per 1,000 population; Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) — infant deaths per 1,000 live births; Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) — maternal deaths per 1,00,000 live births.

question: "The blue umbrella" is a novel written by famous Indian author ______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ruskin Bond.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Blue Umbrella" (1980) is a short novel by Ruskin Bond, set in a village in Himachal Pradesh, about a little girl Binya and her prized blue umbrella. (रस्किन बॉन्ड)

• It was made into a Hindi film (2005) directed by Vishal Bhardwaj, which won the National Film Award for Best Children's Film.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other works of Ruskin Bond: "The Room on the Roof" (which won him the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize at 21), "A Flight of Pigeons" (filmed as Junoon), "The Night Train at Deoli", "Rusty" series.

• He received the Sahitya Akademi Award (1992), the Padma Shri (1999) and the Padma Bhushan (2014). He lives in Landour, Mussoorie.

NOTE

• Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote Devdas, Parineeta and Srikanta in Bengali; Khushwant Singh wrote Train to Pakistan; Arundhati Roy wrote The God of Small Things.

question: ______ are formed when an opaque objects comes in the path of light.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shadows.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "shadow" is formed when an opaque object obstructs the path of light, because light travels in straight lines (rectilinear propagation) and cannot bend around the object. (छाया)

• Three things are needed to form a shadow: a source of light, an opaque object and a screen/surface.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Opaque objects do not allow light to pass through (wood, metal, stone) and form dark, sharp shadows.

• Translucent objects allow light to pass partially (frosted glass, butter paper) and form faint shadows.

• Transparent objects allow light to pass through completely (clear glass, air, water) and form no distinct shadow.

NOTE

• With an extended light source a shadow has two parts: the umbra (complete darkness) and the penumbra (partial shadow).

• Solar and lunar eclipses are natural examples of shadows: in a solar eclipse the Moon's shadow falls on the Earth; in a lunar eclipse the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.

question: Which ministry organised a month-long programme called the 'Kashi Tamil Sangamam' in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Education.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The month-long "Kashi Tamil Sangamam" was organised in 2022 by the Ministry of Education, Government of India, in collaboration with the Ministry of Culture and the Government of Uttar Pradesh. (काशी तमिल संगमम् — शिक्षा मंत्रालय)

• It was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 17 November 2022 at Varanasi (Kashi) and ran till 16 December 2022.

• Its aim was to celebrate and rediscover the age-old cultural, literary and civilisational links between Kashi (Uttar Pradesh) and Tamil Nadu, in the spirit of "Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• IIT Madras and BHU (Banaras Hindu University) were the implementing agencies for the programme.

• A second edition, Kashi Tamil Sangamam 2.0, was held in December 2023.

NOTE

• "Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat" was launched in 2015 on the 140th birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel to promote engagement between states.

• A similar initiative, "Saurashtra Tamil Sangamam", was held in Gujarat in April 2023.

question: Who received the Nobel Prize in Literature 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Annie Ernaux.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Nobel Prize in Literature 2022 was awarded to the French writer Annie Ernaux "for the courage and clinical acuity with which she uncovers the roots, estrangements and collective restraints of personal memory". (एनी एर्नो — साहित्य का नोबेल 2022)

• Her best-known works include "Les Annees (The Years)", "La Place" and "A Woman's Story".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Recent Literature laureates: 2019 — Peter Handke (Austria), 2018 — Olga Tokarczuk (Poland), 2021 — Abdulrazak Gurnah (Tanzania/UK), 2020 — Louise Gluck (USA), 2023 — Jon Fosse (Norway).

• Rabindranath Tagore is the only Indian to win the Nobel Prize in Literature (1913, for Gitanjali).

NOTE

• The Nobel Prizes were instituted from the will of Alfred Nobel and first awarded in 1901. Literature, Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine and Economics prizes are awarded in Stockholm; the Peace Prize in Oslo, Norway.

question: Who among the following is famous for playing the musical instrument 'Sitar'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vilayat Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Vilayat Khan (1928-2004) was one of India's greatest sitar maestros. (उस्ताद विलायत खाँ — सितार)

• He belonged to the Imdadkhani (Etawah) gharana and is credited with developing the "gayaki ang" — a style of sitar playing that imitates the nuances of the human voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Zakir Hussain — legendary tabla player, son of Ustad Alla Rakha; recipient of the Padma Vibhushan and multiple Grammy Awards.

• Ali Akbar Khan — famous sarod player, son of Baba Allauddin Khan.

• Other renowned sitar players: Pandit Ravi Shankar, Nikhil Banerjee, Shahid Parvez and Anoushka Shankar.

NOTE

• The sitar is a plucked string (tat vadya) instrument. Instruments are classified as tat (string), sushir (wind), avanaddha (membrane/percussion) and ghan (solid/metal).

• Instrument–artist pairs: Flute — Hariprasad Chaurasia; Shehnai — Bismillah Khan; Santoor — Shivkumar Sharma; Sarangi — Ram Narayan; Violin — L. Subramaniam.

question: International year of freshwater was observed in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2003.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The United Nations General Assembly declared 2003 as the "International Year of Freshwater". (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय स्वच्छ जल वर्ष — 2003)

• The objective was to raise global awareness about the protection and sustainable management of freshwater resources, and to encourage action towards the water-related Millennium Development Goals.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Only about 2.5% of the Earth's water is freshwater, and most of it is locked in glaciers and ice caps; less than 1% is readily accessible for human use.

• World Water Day is observed every year on 22 March; the UN also declared 2005–2015 as the International Decade for Action, "Water for Life".

NOTE

• Other UN observances: 2008 — International Year of Sanitation, 2013 — Year of Water Cooperation, 2023 — Year of Millets (proposed by India).

• India's water bodies: the Ganga is the longest river within India; Wular Lake (J&K) is the largest freshwater lake in India.
